title: Apply for or renew a concealed handgun permit
question: I live in Staunton and want a concealed handgun permit. Where and how do I apply?
office: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office (Clerk of the Circuit Court, an elected constitutional officer; 25th Judicial Circuit of Virginia)
summary: Staunton residents 21 or older apply to the Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 3rd floor of the Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street, on State Police form SP-248. First-time applicants come in person with a photo ID issued by a Virginia government agency, the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. State Department (passport), and proof of in-person handgun training. Renewals can be mailed with copies of your ID and current permit; for the new permit to start when the old one ends, the court must receive the renewal 90 to 180 days before expiry. The fee is $50 (cards $2 more). The court checks your record and must mail a five-year permit within 45 days unless it finds you disqualified; if it has done neither, the clerk sends a 90-day de facto permit. Only a judge can deny: ask for a hearing within 21 days, then appeal to the Court of Appeals.

legal_basis.quote: The prohibition against carrying a concealed handgun in clause (i) of subsection A of § 18.2-308 shall not apply to a person who has a valid concealed handgun permit issued pursuant to this article.
Any person 21 years of age or older may apply in writing or electronically to the clerk of the circuit court of the county or city in which he resides
There shall be no requirement regarding the length of time an applicant has been a resident or domiciliary of the county or city.

The application shall be on a form prescribed by the Department of State Police, in consultation with the Supreme Court, requiring only that information necessary to determine eligibility for the permit.
The applicant shall present one valid form of photo identification issued by a governmental agency of the Commonwealth or by the U.S. Department of Defense or U.S. State Department (passport).
No information or documentation other than that which is allowed on the application in accordance with this section may be requested or required by the clerk or the court.
The court shall require proof that the applicant has demonstrated competence with a handgun in person
no applicant is required to submit to any additional demonstration of competence, nor shall any proof of demonstrated competence expire
The making of a materially false statement in an application under this article constitutes perjury
The clerk of court shall withhold from public disclosure the applicant's name and any other information contained in a permit application or any order issuing a concealed handgun permit
An application is deemed complete when all information required to be furnished by the applicant, including the fee for a concealed handgun permit
a member of the United States Armed Forces is domiciled in the county or city where such member claims his home of record with the United States Armed Forces
The clerk shall charge a fee of $10 for the processing of an application or issuing of a permit, including his costs associated with the consultation with law-enforcement agencies.
The local law-enforcement agency conducting the background investigation may charge a fee not to exceed $35 to cover the cost of conducting an investigation pursuant to this article.
The State Police may charge a fee not to exceed $5 to cover its costs associated with processing the application.
The total amount assessed for processing an application for a permit shall not exceed $50, with such fees to be paid in one sum to the person who receives the application.
Payment may be made by any method accepted by that court for payment of other fees or penalties.
No payment shall be required until the application is received by the court as a complete application.
No fee shall be charged for the issuance of such permit to a person who has retired from service
The clerk of court shall enter on the application the date on which the application and all other information required to be submitted by the applicant is received.
Upon receipt of the completed application, the court shall consult with either the sheriff or police department of the county or city and receive a report from the Central Criminal Records Exchange.

The court shall issue the permit via United States mail and notify the State Police of the issuance of the permit within 45 days of receipt of the completed application unless it is determined that the applicant is disqualified.
A court may authorize the clerk to issue concealed handgun permits, without judicial review, to applicants who have submitted complete applications

the clerk shall certify on the application that the 45-day period has expired, and mail or send via electronic mail a copy of the certified application to the applicant within five business days of the expiration of the 45-day period
The certified application shall serve as a de facto permit, which shall expire 90 days after issuance
the disqualification shall be deemed a denial of the permit and a revocation of the de facto permit

The State Police shall enter the permittee's name and description in the Virginia Criminal Information Network so that the permit's existence and current status will be made known to law-enforcement personnel accessing the Network for investigative purposes.
Only a circuit court judge may deny issuance of a concealed handgun permit to a Virginia resident or domiciliary
the clerk shall provide notice, in writing, upon denial of the application, of the applicant's right to an ore tenus hearing and the requirements for perfecting an appeal of such order
Upon request of the applicant made within 21 days, the court shall place the matter on the docket for an ore tenus hearing.
The applicant may be represented by counsel, but counsel shall not be appointed, and the rules of evidence shall apply.
Any person denied a permit to carry a concealed handgun by the circuit court may appeal to the Court of Appeals.

Such person shall file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the circuit court noting an appeal to the Court of Appeals and file his opening brief with the Court of Appeals within 60 days of the expiration of the time for requesting an ore tenus hearing, or if an ore tenus hearing is requested, within 60 days of the entry of the final order of the circuit court following the hearing.
if the decision to deny the permit is reversed upon appeal, taxable costs incurred by the person shall be paid by the Commonwealth
The decision of the Court of Appeals or judge shall be final.
The following persons shall be deemed disqualified from obtaining a permit:
An individual who has been convicted of two or more misdemeanors within the five-year period immediately preceding the application, if one of the misdemeanors was a Class 1 misdemeanor
An individual who has a felony charge pending or a charge pending for an offense listed in subdivision 14 or 15.

Persons who previously have been issued a concealed handgun permit pursuant to this article shall not be required to appear in person to apply for a new five-year permit pursuant to this section, and the application for the new permit, including a photocopy of the applicant's valid photo identification, may be submitted via the United States mail.
The circuit court that receives the application shall promptly notify an applicant if the application is incomplete or if the fee submitted for the permit pursuant to § 18.2-308.03 is incorrect.
provided that the application is received by the court at least 90 days but no more than 180 days prior to the expiration of the existing permit
Any order denying issuance of the new permit shall be in accordance with subsection A of § 18.2-308.08
such permit shall remain valid for 90 days after the end date of the deployment

The failure of a clerk to send the notice required by this subsection or the failure of the permit holder to receive such notice shall not extend the validity of the existing permit beyond its expiration date.
The total amount assessed for processing a replacement permit pursuant to this subsection shall not exceed $10
The clerk shall issue the replacement permit within 10 business days of receiving the notarized statement and may charge a fee not to exceed $5.

shall display the permit and a photo identification issued by a government agency of the Commonwealth or by the U.S. Department of Defense or U.S. State Department (passport) upon demand by a law-enforcement officer
Failure to display the permit and a photo identification upon demand by a law-enforcement officer shall be punishable by a $25 civil penalty

The granting of a concealed handgun permit pursuant to this article shall not thereby authorize the possession of any handgun or other weapon on property or in places where such possession is otherwise prohibited by law or is prohibited by the owner of private property.
It is unlawful for any person to possess in or transport into any courthouse in this Commonwealth any (i) gun or other weapon designed or intended to propel a missile or projectile of any kind

The clerk of any circuit court shall not be required to but may, in his discretion, accept credit or debit card payment in lieu of money to collect and secure all fees, including filing fees, fines, restitution, forfeitures, penalties, and costs collected.

may add to such payment a sum not to exceed four percent of the amount paid for the transaction, or a flat fee not to exceed $2 per transaction, as a reasonable convenience fee for the acceptance of a credit or debit card
its decision shall be final, without appeal to the Supreme Court, in:
For filing a notice of appeal or initiating any matter under the original jurisdiction of the court, $50 payable by check or money order to the Clerk of the Court of Appeals.
a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals in any case within the jurisdiction of the court shall be filed within 30 days from the date of any final judgment order, decree, or conviction

application for a writ of mandamus or a writ of prohibition shall be on petition verified by oath, after the party against whom the writ is prayed has been served with a copy of the petition and notice of the intended application a reasonable time before such application is made

The petition shall state plainly and concisely the grounds of the application, concluding with a prayer for the writ, and shall be presented to the court having jurisdiction, unless the application is to the Court of Appeals or the Supreme Court.

legal_basis.citation: Staunton City Code § 9.05.280 (Application for a concealed handgun permit – Fingerprinting), repealed by Ord. 2012-08; on eCode360, not quoted under its terms (see caveats)

steps.step: Check that you can apply in Staunton
steps.how: You must be at least 21 and live in the City of Staunton. There is no minimum time you must have lived here. A member of the U.S. Armed Forces stationed outside Virginia applies where he or she is domiciled, which is the home of record with the Armed Forces. If you live in Augusta County or Waynesboro, even with a Staunton mailing address, apply to that circuit court instead. You must not fall under any of the 20 disqualifications in Va. Code § 18.2-308.09. Among them: being barred from having a firearm; being subject to a protective order; a pending felony charge; two or more misdemeanors in the last five years if one was Class 1; DUI or public drunkenness, assault, or a drug offense in the last three years; stalking; or residential mental-health or substance-abuse treatment in the last five years.
steps.quote: Applicants must reside in the City of Staunton.

steps.step: Get proof that you showed handgun competence in person (first-time applicants)
steps.how: Get a photocopy of a certificate of completion, an affidavit from the instructor or school, or another document showing you did one of the things § 18.2-308.02(B) accepts. These are: a hunter education course approved by the Department of Wildlife Resources (or another state's agency); an NRA or USCCA firearms safety or training course; a public class from a law-enforcement agency, college or firearms school whose instructors are NRA-, USCCA- or DCJS-certified; a law-enforcement or security-guard firearms course; organized shooting competition, current military service or an honorable discharge; a Virginia or local license to carry that you held before and was not revoked for cause; an in-person course with a state-, NRA- or USCCA-certified instructor; a police agency's firearms qualification; or other training the court finds adequate. Staunton's page asks for proof of in-person training, or a copy of a current concealed handgun permit. The proof never expires, and the court may not demand any further demonstration.
steps.quote: The court shall require proof that the applicant has demonstrated competence with a handgun in person

steps.step: Fill in the State Police application, Form SP-248
steps.how: Download the application, Form SP-248 (revised 11-24-2025), from the Virginia State Police; one form serves resident, nonresident and renewal applicants. The copy now on the State Police page is fillable. Tick Resident Permit, and Renewal as well if you are renewing. The form asks for your full legal name (with a separate list of any other names you have used), date of birth, home address (with a list of every address in the last five years), physical description, place of birth, citizenship and phone. It then asks yes/no questions about disqualifying history, with Forms 1 and 2 on page 2 to explain any charges, convictions or mental-health orders, and asks whether you now hold a Virginia resident permit and from which court. Your Social Security number and email address are optional; to get an electronic notice before the permit expires, give an email address and tick the box for that notice. First-time applicants attach a photocopy of their proof of competence (s2). Sign and date it. A materially false statement is perjury. The clerk and the court may not ask for information or documents beyond what the form allows. The State Police say questions about filling in the form, residency or proof of competence go to the court.
steps.quote: The application shall be on a form prescribed by the Department of State Police, in consultation with the Supreme Court, requiring only that information necessary to determine eligibility for the permit.

steps.step: First-time applicants: file in person at the Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.who: You (the applicant); Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Bring the completed SP-248, your proof of in-person training, a valid photo ID and the fee to the Clerk's Office. It is on the 3rd floor of the George M. Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street, and is open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. State law calls for one valid photo ID issued by a Virginia government agency, the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. State Department (a passport); the City page says only 'a valid photo I.D.'. Do not bring a handgun or any other weapon: the Clerk's Visitor Information page says no weapons of any sort are permitted in the building, and carrying a gun into any courthouse is a Class 1 misdemeanor (§ 18.2-283.1), with or without a permit. Phones, tablets, computers and other electronic devices are not permitted in the building either. The Staunton Circuit Court's Portable Electronic Devices Policy (adopted June 2026) makes exceptions for some groups, such as attorneys, and provides free storage at the security entrance for visitors who may not bring a device in; the Sheriff is not liable for loss or damage.
steps.deadline: Transactions requiring payment must be done before 4:30 p.m.
steps.quote: All first-time applicants must appear in person with a valid photo I.D. and proof of in- person firearms training.

steps.step: Renewals: mail or bring your application within the renewal window
steps.who: You (a current or former permit holder)
steps.how: If you have been issued a Virginia resident permit before, you do not have to come in person. Mail or bring the SP-248 marked Renewal, a copy of your valid photo ID, a copy of your current permit and the $50 fee to the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 113 E. Beverley Street, Staunton, VA 24401. The City page says checks can be made payable to Clerk of Court; it does not say how to pay by card for a mailed renewal, so a check or money order is the simple choice by mail (a suggestion, not an office rule). Like a new application, a renewal goes to the court where you live now. Aim for the court to receive it 90 to 180 days before your permit expires: then the new five-year permit starts on the day the old one expires. You get an email notice at least 90 days before expiry only if the clerk's system can send one and you asked for it on the form, and a missed notice does not extend your permit. If you serve in the Virginia National Guard or the U.S. Armed Forces or Reserves and your permit expires while you are deployed on active duty outside Staunton, it stays valid for 90 days after the deployment ends; carry, and show an officer on request, a copy of your deployment orders or other papers from your commanding officer that give the start and end dates. The court must tell you promptly if a renewal is incomplete or the fee is wrong. Only a judge can refuse a renewal, under the same rules as a denial (s10).
steps.deadline: For the new permit to start when the old one expires, the court must receive the application at least 90 days but no more than 180 days before the current permit expires
steps.quote: Renewal applications may be provided in person or mailed with a copy of a valid photo I.D. and a copy of the applicants current permit.

steps.who: You (the applicant); Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Pay the $50 in one sum when you file, by cash, check, money order or credit card. The City page says checks can be made payable to Clerk of Court. Card payments carry a $2.00 surcharge. State law caps the total at $50: $10 for the clerk, up to $35 for the local sheriff or police background investigation, and up to $5 for the State Police. Some retirees pay nothing: retired magistrates, and retired law-enforcement officers (including Virginia ABC special agents), Coast Guard boarding officers, correctional officers and probation and parole officers who meet the service rules in § 18.2-308.03(B) (generally 15 years of service, or for some age 55). State law also says no payment is required until the court has a complete application.
steps.deadline: When you file; in person, before 4:30 p.m.
steps.quote: A $50 filing fee is required upon submission of application and may be made payable by cash, check, money order or credit card.

steps.step: The clerk dates your application and the court runs the background check
steps.who: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office; Staunton Circuit Court; the City Sheriff or the Staunton Police Department; Virginia State Police (Central Criminal Records Exchange)
steps.how: The clerk writes on your application the date it and everything else required were received. That date starts the 45-day clock. An application is complete once all the required information and the fee are in. The court then consults the sheriff or the police department and gets a report from the State Police's Central Criminal Records Exchange. The sheriff, the chief of police or the Commonwealth's Attorney may give the court a sworn statement that you are likely to use a weapon unlawfully or negligently. The court may let the clerk issue permits to clean applications without a judge's review. The clerk must keep your name and application details out of public view.
steps.deadline: The 45-day period runs from the receipt date the clerk writes on the application
steps.quote: Upon receipt of the completed application, the court shall consult with either the sheriff or police department of the county or city and receive a report from the Central Criminal Records Exchange.

steps.step: Receive your five-year permit by mail, and carry it with photo ID
steps.who: Staunton Circuit Court (issues and mails the permit); you
steps.how: If you are not disqualified, the court mails you the five-year permit and tells the State Police, which enters it in the Virginia Criminal Information Network. The permit shows your name, address, date of birth, gender, height, weight, hair and eye color and signature, the signature of the judge or of an authorized clerk, the issue date and the expiry date. Whenever you carry a concealed handgun, you must have the permit on you, and when a law-enforcement officer asks, you must show it with a photo ID issued by a Virginia government agency, the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. State Department (passport). Failing to show them is punishable by a $25 civil penalty, which a court may waive if you then present a valid permit and a government-issued photo ID. The permit does not let you carry where the law or a private owner forbids it, for example in any courthouse.
steps.deadline: Within 45 days of receipt of the completed application
steps.quote: The court shall issue the permit via United States mail and notify the State Police of the issuance of the permit within 45 days of receipt of the completed application unless it is determined that the applicant is disqualified.

steps.step: If 45 days pass with no decision, the clerk sends you a de facto permit
steps.how: Suppose the court has neither issued the permit nor found you disqualified within 45 days of the receipt date on your application. Then the clerk must certify on the application that the 45 days have passed, and mail or email you a copy within five business days. Shown with a valid government photo ID, the certified copy works as a permit for 90 days, or until the court issues the five-year permit or finds you disqualified. If you are later found disqualified, you must surrender it to the court, and that counts as a denial (with the hearing and appeal rights in s10).
steps.deadline: The clerk sends the certified application within five business days after the 45-day period ends; it expires 90 days after issuance
steps.quote: The certified application shall serve as a de facto permit, which shall expire 90 days after issuance

steps.step: If you are denied, ask for a hearing within 21 days, then appeal
steps.who: A Staunton Circuit Court judge; the Clerk's Office (written notice); you
steps.how: Only a circuit court judge can deny a Virginia resident. The order must say why, naming any § 18.2-308.09 disqualification. The clerk must tell you in writing about your right to an ore tenus hearing (a live hearing in court) and how to appeal. Ask for the hearing within 21 days (the court section of the SP-248 says within 21 days of the denial). You may bring a lawyer, but none will be appointed, and the rules of evidence apply. The court's final order must include its findings of fact and conclusions of law. After that, you can appeal to the Court of Appeals of Virginia (see escalation).
steps.deadline: Request the ore tenus hearing within 21 days of the denial
steps.quote: Only a circuit court judge may deny issuance of a concealed handgun permit to a Virginia resident or domiciliary

steps.step: Later: get a replacement permit if you move, lose it or change your name
steps.who: You (the permit holder); the Circuit Court Clerk's Office that issued the permit
steps.how: The State Police say a permit stays valid after you move, but you may ask for a replacement that shows your new address. Give the clerk of the court that issued the permit your valid permit and State Police Form SP-248A. The total charge may not exceed $10. If the permit was lost or destroyed, or you changed your name legally, give the clerk a notarized statement. The clerk then issues a replacement with the same expiry date within 10 business days, for no more than $5. Staunton's actual replacement fees were not found.
steps.deadline: Lost, destroyed or name change: the clerk issues the replacement within 10 business days of receiving the notarized statement
steps.fee: Change of address: not more than $10 in total; lost, destroyed or name change: not more than $5
steps.quote: The clerk of a circuit court that issued a valid concealed handgun permit shall, upon presentation by the permit holder of the valid permit and written notice of a change of address on a form provided by the Department of State Police, issue a replacement permit specifying the permit holder's new address.

escalation.trigger: No permit and no finding of disqualification 45 days after the clerk received your complete application
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, which must certify the application and mail or email you a copy; the certified copy is a 90-day de facto permit (s9)
escalation.deadline: Within five business days after the 45-day period ends; the de facto permit lasts 90 days
escalation.quote: the clerk shall certify on the application that the 45-day period has expired, and mail or send via electronic mail a copy of the certified application to the applicant within five business days of the expiration of the 45-day period

escalation.trigger: The Clerk's Office asks for information or documents that the SP-248 form does not call for (beyond the photo ID and the proof of competence)
escalation.next: Raise it with the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, pointing to § 18.2-308.02(A). If the office still refuses to accept or date a complete application, see the mandamus rung below
escalation.quote: No information or documentation other than that which is allowed on the application in accordance with this section may be requested or required by the clerk or the court.

escalation.trigger: The clerk will not accept or date a complete application, or does not send the de facto permit when the 45 days run out
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court: a petition for a writ of mandamus against the clerk, verified by oath, stating the grounds and asking for the writ, served with notice on the clerk a reasonable time before it is presented. This is the general remedy to compel a public officer's duty, not one written for permits; consider a lawyer
escalation.deadline: Serve the petition and notice a reasonable time before the application is made
escalation.quote: application for a writ of mandamus or a writ of prohibition shall be on petition verified by oath, after the party against whom the writ is prayed has been served with a copy of the petition and notice of the intended application a reasonable time before such application is made

escalation.trigger: A judge denies the permit or the renewal
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court: an ore tenus (live) hearing. You may bring a lawyer, none is appointed, and the rules of evidence apply
escalation.quote: Upon request of the applicant made within 21 days, the court shall place the matter on the docket for an ore tenus hearing.

escalation.trigger: The court later finds you disqualified after sending a de facto permit
escalation.next: Surrender the de facto permit to the court. The finding counts as a denial, so the hearing and appeal rungs apply
escalation.quote: the disqualification shall be deemed a denial of the permit and a revocation of the de facto permit

escalation.trigger: The denial stands after the hearing, or you did not ask for a hearing
escalation.next: Court of Appeals of Virginia: file a notice of appeal with the Staunton Circuit Court clerk and an opening brief, with copies of the circuit court papers and the denial order, with the Court of Appeals ($50 filing fee). Its decision is final, with no appeal to the Supreme Court of Virginia (§ 17.1-410(A)(3)). If the denial is reversed, the Commonwealth pays your taxable costs
escalation.deadline: Within 60 days of the end of the 21-day hearing window, or of the final order after the hearing. The general 30-day rule for notices of appeal (§ 8.01-675.3) may also apply to the notice; see caveats
escalation.quote: Any person denied a permit to carry a concealed handgun by the circuit court may appeal to the Court of Appeals.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Visitor Information page is its copy of 2025-11-15. The pages of vacourts.gov, vsp.virginia.gov and law.lis.virginia.gov were read live. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Form link: the City page (2026-05-11) links an SP-248 copy at vsp.virginia.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ (Rev. 11-24-2025; it still loads, but has no fillable fields). The State Police page now links a fillable copy of the same revision at /2026/07/ (f1). The text of the two differs only in layout. The 2025-11-15 capture of the City page linked the State Police page instead.

Electronic filing: since 2026 Acts c. 1034 (HB 101), § 18.2-308.02(A) lets a person apply 'in writing or electronically'. The effective date of that chapter was not checked. The City page (May 2026 capture) describes only in-person filing for first-time applicants and in-person or mailed renewals. No online channel was found for Staunton. Ask the Clerk's Office whether it accepts electronic applications.

Photo ID: the City page asks for 'a valid photo I.D.' But § 18.2-308.02(A) names only photo ID issued by a Virginia government agency, the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. State Department (passport). An out-of-state driver's license may not be accepted.

Competence list: the State Police page gives option 2 as a handgun class teaching concealed carry for self-defense outside the home, state handgun laws and safe storage. The Code text in Open US Law's copy, and on LIS on 2026-10-11, gives option 2 as 'Completing any National Rifle Association or United States Concealed Carry Association firearms safety or training course'. This page follows the Code text. LIS shows no delayed-effective version of § 18.2-308.02, and other parts of the State Police page are out of date (it still describes a 'petition for review' and cites 'former Section 37.1-134.1'), so its option 2 wording is not relied on. Ask the Clerk's Office if your training is of the kind the State Police page describes.

Appeal procedure: the State Police page and Notice 3 of the SP-248 describe a 'petition for review' to the Court of Appeals. That is the procedure before 2021 Sp. Sess. I c. 489. The current § 18.2-308.08(C) calls for a notice of appeal filed with the circuit court clerk and an opening brief filed with the Court of Appeals 'within 60 days' of the end of the hearing window or of the final order. It is not clear whether the 60 days also governs the notice of appeal, or whether the general rule in § 8.01-675.3 applies (a notice of appeal within 30 days of a final judgment). To be safe, file the notice within 30 days of the final order. The Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (Part 5A) were not read. Consider a lawyer.

Which local agency runs the background check was not found. Staunton has both a City Sheriff and a Police Department, and the Code says the court consults 'either the sheriff or police department'. It was also not found whether that agency charges the full $35. The City's single $50 fee equals the statutory maximum ($10 + $35 + $5).

Not found: whether the Staunton Circuit Court has authorized the clerk to issue permits for clean applications without judicial review (§ 18.2-308.04(D)); typical processing times; whether the clerk can send expiry reminders by email (§ 18.2-308.010(C)); and the City's actual replacement-permit fees (the state caps are given).

The City page says the fee is 'required upon submission of application'. § 18.2-308.03(A) says no payment is required until the court receives a complete application. In practice the two coincide when you file a complete application.

Renewals: the City asks for a copy of the current permit as well as the photo ID. State law lists only a photocopy of the photo ID for mailed renewals, but a license to carry held before is itself accepted proof of competence (§ 18.2-308.02(B)(6)), which may be why the copy is asked for.

Local law: Staunton City Code § 9.05.280, 'Application for a concealed handgun permit – Fingerprinting', is on eCode360 (General Code). The Terms of Use limit the content to personal use and forbid reproducing it for public purposes, so it is not quoted. Paraphrase: the section is shown as repealed by Ord. 2012-08; its history note cites the 2003 reformat, an ordinance of 6-24-97 and 1985 Code § 18-36. No current local ordinance on concealed handgun permits was found in Title 9 (Public Peace, Morals and Welfare). eCode360 warns its copy may not reflect the latest legislation. The resident sections of the Code cited here (§§ 18.2-308.02 to 18.2-308.05) set no fingerprint requirement; § 18.2-308.03 mentions fingerprints only for nonresident applicants.

Not confirmed: the City's 'Augusta, Staunton, and Waynesboro Concealed Handgun Permit Training Press Release 2021' (showpublisheddocument/9889), which has no Internet Archive copy, and the City's own 'Policy Regarding Portable Electronic Devices' (showpublisheddocument/9568), linked from the Visitor Information page. The Staunton Circuit Court's Portable Electronic Devices Policy on vacourts.gov (adopted 6/10/2026) is a scan with no text layer, so it is paraphrased, not quoted. It bars portable electronic devices from the courthouse except for listed groups (attorneys; law enforcement, probation officers and magistrates on duty; judges; City and State employees with credentials on official business; court reporters; Department of Forensic Science employees attending as witnesses; interpreters; and other visitors when the Sheriff determines they pose no security risk and need the device for their business or their case). It provides free storage at the security entrance, at no cost, and the Sheriff is not liable for loss or damage. It revokes the court's earlier device policies, so the City's older policy may be superseded. The signing judge's name is not recorded.

Residence decides the court. Augusta County and the City of Waynesboro have their own circuit courts. Someone with a Staunton mailing address who lives in Augusta County applies to the Augusta County Circuit Court, not to Staunton.

The disqualifications are summarized in s1. Read § 18.2-308.09 in full before applying; Open US Law's copy includes its 2026 amendments (cc. 1106, 1107). This page does not cover nonresident permits (filed with the State Police under § 18.2-308.06), retired law-enforcement officers' carry rights (§ 18.2-308.016), or suspension and revocation (§ 18.2-308.013).
The State Police FAQ says a resident permit remains valid after a change of address. The Code makes the address-change replacement available but does not say a move invalidates the permit.
No staff names or individual contact details are recorded; the Clerk's Office channels are taken from its City page, the Public Records Request page and vacourts.gov.

corrections: Quotes: all 83 original quotes are verbatim, and one was added (84 in all). The 78 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section, with whitespace normalised only (index rows 5432-5434, 5440-5443, 5445-5447, 5406, 6086, 4668, 4676, 30346, 30322 and 30324), and the subsection labels match the text. lexflow's own matcher (places.check_quotes) reports 78 of 78 code quotes matched and 6 other. The 6 City quotes were matched word for word (the page's non-breaking spaces read as spaces) in both Internet Archive captures of the Concealed Weapons Permit page, 2026-05-11 and 2025-11-15. The live City site still answers HTTP 403 to the research client, robots.txt included, and was not fetched another way. vsp.virginia.gov, vacourts.gov and law.lis.virginia.gov were re-read read-only with the lexflow User-Agent, at least one second apart per host, and their robots.txt files allow the pages read.

Summary: 'a Virginia or federal photo ID' was broader than § 18.2-308.02(A), which names photo ID issued by a Virginia government agency, the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. State Department (passport); it now names those three. 'File 90 to 180 days before expiry' read as a filing deadline; § 18.2-308.010(A)(2) makes the window the condition for the new permit to start when the old one expires, and the summary now says so. 'Must mail a five-year permit within 45 days, or the clerk sends a 90-day de facto permit' left out the disqualification exception in § 18.2-308.04(C) and the condition in § 18.2-308.05; both are now stated.

Step s3: the SP-248 (11-24-2025) asks you to give an email address and tick a box to request the electronic expiry notice; giving an email alone does not request it. The step now says so, says to tick Resident Permit (and Renewal when renewing), and adds the form's list of other names, question O (a current Virginia resident permit and its court) and item 9 (a photocopy of the proof of competence, initial permits only).

Step s4: 'Leave your phone, tablet and computer behind' was not the whole rule. The Staunton Circuit Court's Portable Electronic Devices Policy (vacourts.gov, adopted 6/10/2026) was read as an image (scan, no text layer, so not quoted): it makes exceptions for listed groups and provides free storage at the security entrance, with the Sheriff not liable for loss or damage. The step now says so. 'State law accepts only' became 'State law calls for', with the City page's own wording kept apart. The weapons rule now cites the Visitor Information page ('No weapons of any sort') and § 18.2-283.1, which applies with or without a permit (§ 18.2-308.01(C)).

Step s5: 'by mail, a check or money order payable to Clerk of Court' read as a City rule. The page lists cash, check, money order or credit card and says only that checks can be made payable to Clerk of Court; it gives no rule for mailed payments. The step now says this and labels the check-or-money-order advice as a suggestion. The deployment rule now names who it covers (Virginia National Guard, U.S. Armed Forces or Reserves) and the documents to carry and show, as § 18.2-308.010(B) does. The expiry notice is now 'at least 90 days' before expiry (§ 18.2-308.010(C)). 'Held a Virginia permit before' became 'been issued a Virginia resident permit before' (§ 18.2-308.010(A)(1), 'issued a concealed handgun permit pursuant to this article').

Step s6 and the retiree fee row: § 18.2-308.03(B)(ii) also covers retired Virginia ABC special agents, and the fee row left out Coast Guard boarding officers (clause vi). Both are now listed. 'Make checks payable to Clerk of Court' now follows the City page's 'can be made payable'.

Step s8: § 18.2-308.01(A) requires the permit on your person at all times while carrying, and the permit plus a photo ID from a Virginia government agency, the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. State Department to be shown on demand. The step said 'a government photo ID', which is broader; it now names the three issuers. It also adds the court's power to waive the $25 civil penalty (§ 18.2-308.01(B)) and the judge's or authorized clerk's signature on the permit (§ 18.2-308.04(E)).

Step s10: the 21 days run from the denial, as the court section of the SP-248 states (a hearing request within twenty-one days of the denial); § 18.2-308.08(B) alone does not say. The step and its deadline now say so.

Legal basis: the citations 'Va. Code § 18.2-308.010(A(1))', '(A(2))' and '(A(3))' are now written (A)(1), (A)(2) and (A)(3). Added the sentence of § 18.2-308.08(C), 'The decision of the Court of Appeals or judge shall be final.', which, with § 17.1-410(A)(3) (confirmed: 'Appeals involving denial of a concealed handgun permit pursuant to § 18.2-308.08'), supports the escalation's statement that the Court of Appeals decision is final.

Caveats and sources: the archive serves the 2025-11-15 capture of the Visitor Information page for the 2026-05-11 timestamp, and the source title and first caveat now say so. The 'Not read' caveat now records the court's 2026 device policy as read (paraphrased, judge not named) and the City's older policy (showpublisheddocument/9568) as not read. The competence caveat now records that LIS shows no delayed-effective version of § 18.2-308.02 and that the State Police page is out of date elsewhere. The device policy was added to sources.

Legal review: every other step, deadline, fee and escalation rung was compared with the cited text and found consistent, with 'may' and 'shall' kept. That covers § 18.2-308.02(A)-(F) (age, residence or military domicile, no length-of-residence rule, the form, no extra documents, the competence list as the Code gives it, perjury, confidentiality, completeness); § 18.2-308.03(A) ($10 clerk, up to $35 local, up to $5 State Police, $50 cap in one sum, no payment until complete); § 18.2-308.04(A)-(D) (receipt date, consultation and CCRE report, 45 days by mail, the court 'may' authorize clerk issuance); § 18.2-308.05 (certification within five business days, a 90-day de facto permit, surrender on disqualification); §§ 18.2-308.07(A), 18.2-308.08(A)-(C), 18.2-308.09 (20 disqualifications; the s1 summary matches subdivisions 1, 5-7, 9, 14, 15, 17-19), 18.2-308.010 and 18.2-308.011 (the State Police FAQ confirms that a permit stays valid after a move; the SP-248A is for address changes only, and the notarized statement covers loss and name change); § 19.2-353.3 (the $2.00 card surcharge is within the cap); §§ 17.1-410(A)(3), 17.1-418(1), 8.01-675.3, 8.01-644 and 8.01-645. The Clerk's Office is the right office (§ 18.2-308.02(A); SP-248 Notice 2). The State Police page's 'petition for review' and its option-2 wording are not followed, since the Code differs. Local rules (residence in the City, in-person first filing, the copy of the current permit for renewals, payment methods, the surcharge, checks to Clerk of Court, hours, payment before 4:30 p.m. and building rules) are attributed to the City pages and the court's policy, and state rules to the Code.

Completeness against the Concealed Weapons Permit page (2026-05-11 capture): every item on it is covered: residence, the SP-248, proof of in-person competency or a copy of a current permit, the $50 fee and how to pay, the $2.00 card surcharge, checks to Clerk of Court, in-person first applications with photo ID and proof of training, in-person or mailed renewals with copies of the photo ID and the current permit, the mailing address, the State Police link (contacts), the 2021 training press release (not readable; caveat) and the no-electronic-devices note. Both forms (SP-248 (11-24-2025), fillable with 157 widget annotations; SP-248A (7-1-2017), fillable with 16) were re-downloaded, and their numbers, titles and fillable flags match. The older SP-248 copy the City links has no widgets, as the form-link caveat says.

Privacy: the Clerk's City page, vacourts.gov, the Public Records Request page and the court's device policy name the Clerk, judges and staff, and the Public Records Request page lists personal mailboxes for other departments. Cochran Judicial Center' is the building's name.
